title: Multi-temporal assessment of a wildfire chronosequence by remote sensing
author: Nájera De Ferrari, Duarte, et al.
materials: fire recurrence in the same site and

steps.title: Define selection criteria and acquire data
steps.instruction: Compile local vegetation survey information and use GIS tools (QGIS 3.2) together with a digital elevation model (DEM) to define altitude, exposition, and slope; then select medium‑high‑severity burned forest sites spanning a 23‑year period using remote‑sensing burn‑scar severity maps.

substeps.instruction: Gather land‑use survey data for native forest and plantation areas.
Overlay DEM layers to assess topographic constraints.
Apply the selection criteria (Table 3) to identify candidate sites.

steps.title: Analyze burn‑scar severity in GEE
steps.instruction: Import the selected satellite imagery into Google Earth Engine (GEE) and compute the Burn Severity Ratio (dNBR) for each candidate site.

steps.title: Run LandTrendr time‑series analysis
steps.instruction: In GEE, apply the LandTrendr algorithm (Braaten 2021) to the annual Landsat image stack for each site, generating a behavior graph of the Normalized Burn Ratio (NBR) and the derived dNBR indicator.

substeps.instruction: Obtain yearly NBR values for the full 23‑year chronosequence.
Identify fire events as sudden NBR decreases.
Identify vegetation recovery as consistent NBR increases over two to three consecutive years.
Manually inspect and correct graph distortions caused by missing images or cloud cover, corroborating with field observations.

steps.title: Apply discrimination filters
steps.instruction: Exclude sites that meet any of the following criteria: (1) fire recurrence at the same location, (2) land‑use change during the period, or (3) repetitive points within the same forest patch.

steps.title: Select final field sites
steps.instruction: After filtering, retain no more than 20 sites that are ≥2 ha of native forest dominated by a mix of temperate deciduous and evergreen Nothofagus spp. (Roble‑Rauli‑Coigue type) across the defined cluster seasons.

substeps.instruction: Group sites into four cluster seasons: 2023‑2021, 2019‑2017, 2012‑2011, and 2002‑2001.

steps.title: Conduct field sampling
steps.instruction: Visit the selected sites and perform in‑situ soil sampling and vegetation‑cover evaluation.

substeps.instruction: Sample a total of 40 sites (10 sites per season): per season, sample four burned native‑forest sites, four burned pine‑plantation sites, one unburned native‑forest site, and one unburned pine‑plantation site.
Add eight additional sites from the 2005‑2006 season for vegetation analysis on burned native forests and pine plantations.
Record soil type (e.g., Andisols) and note any disturbances such as relief‑derived shadows, clouds, smoke, snow, open land, or abrupt land‑cover conversion.
Use local knowledge of past fire events to adjust site selection and avoid interferences.

steps.title: Validate remote‑sensing results
steps.instruction: Compare field observations (soil properties and vegetation cover) with the remote‑sensing classifications; confirm that at least 80 % of the 40 sampled sites correspond to the sites selected by the computing platform and criteria.
